solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go on about head of root vegetable

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to go on at length is to spout

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone harping on about the top of a root crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the head of 'root', inside SPOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brussels sprout is a green vegetable, the usual short name being this word.

clue.text: Father rounding on innkeeper

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: padre is a title for a chaplain or priest, addressed as Father

explanation.surface: A priest turning on the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: PADRONE is the Italian for a landlord or master, so the definition is fairer than it first looks; 'rounding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italy the owner of a hotel or inn is called by this Italian word for master.

clue.text: Code word used by radio's 'Caroline'?

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A call sign used by the pirate station Radio Caroline.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio Caroline was a famous British pirate radio station.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter O is signalled by this code word.

clue.text: What could make row? Estate car, perhaps

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters may be formed into something new

explanation.surface: Asking what turns a quarrel into an estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges ROW and ESTATE; 'What' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sports car with room for only a driver and passenger is an example.

clue.text: Last, in spite of expectations to the contrary

definitions.meaning: coming after every other one, that is, last of the lot

definitions.text: in spite of expectations to the contrary
definitions.meaning: the phrase used when something happens despite doubts, as in 'he came, ____'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both coming behind everyone else and nevertheless, despite what was expected.

clue.text: Assistant in a small company, reportedly not a heavyweight

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: something not heavy is light

explanation.surface: A junior helper in a small firm, said to be a lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives LYTE, which sounds like LIGHT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who helps a priest at the altar, hence any helper or follower.

clue.text: Pale, Italian climbing, lacking courage

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads the letters upward, so in reverse

parts.note: dim means faint or pale, as of light

explanation.surface: A pale Italian climber with no nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns DIMIT upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and fearful, a synonym for lacking courage.

clue.text: Ice, mostly, on top of old Irish lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first piece above the rest
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: icy reserve is coolness of manner

explanation.surface: Ice sitting on an old lake in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of RESERVE; 'on top of' stacks it over OIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake for storing water.

clue.text: Using few words, endlessly beat a prisoner inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece
endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to lick is to beat or thrash
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: Tersely put: endlessly beating a convict in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lick' is informal for beat or thrash; 'endlessly' trims its last letter and 'inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse and brief, in the Spartan manner.

clue.text: One qualified to make songs better?

definitions.text: One qualified to make songs better?

parts.words: One qualified to make songs better?
parts.note: read literally, someone who fixes up tunes, as one would doctor a text; really the holder of a top academic degree in the subject

explanation.surface: A tune-fixer with credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' as a verb means to tinker with or improve; the clue reads the degree title as a job description.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of the highest university degree in music is formally qualified in that field.

clue.text: Good manners in palace? Yes, all over the place

parts.note: a royal court is a palace and its household

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters of yes are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether manners are good at a royal residence, with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue in two; 'all over the place' is the anagram signal, making ESY.
explanation.definitionFit: Politeness and considerate behaviour are what good manners amount to.

clue.text: Favourite left out? That's brave

indicators.note: out means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a darling is a favourite, as in teacher's darling

explanation.surface: The favourite has been left out of the team, which takes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L (left) from DARLING; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and courageous, a synonym of brave in adjective form.

clue.text: Rumour about harbour

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, used as about
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Gossip going round the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be hearsay or a rumour, as in 'reports of his death'.

clue.text: Not properly adjusted, hence future too unpredictable

indicators.note: unpredictable means the letters fall in no set order

explanation.surface: Things are off-kilter, so the future is too uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpredictable' rearranges FUTURE TOO; 'hence' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of alignment, idiomatically said of a wall or wheel that is not straight.

clue.text: Tread on someone's toes — each corn, unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone treading on toes and hitting a corn every time, ouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges EACH CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on another's territory or rights is idiomatically to tread on their toes.

clue.text: Chapter on posture in Lady Chatterley, for example

parts.note: a stance is a posture

explanation.surface: A chapter on positions in a famous racy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Chatterley, heroine of D. H. Lawrence's novel, is named Constance.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the heroine of Lady Chatterley's Lover, so an example by name.

clue.text: Very strong players attached to golf club

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Actors joining a golf club form a sturdy team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbreakable, like an alibi, is figuratively solid as metal, hence very strong.

clue.text: Piece in paper, tiny piece with no heading

indicators.note: with no heading means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a tiny fragment, with no headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heading' drops the P from PARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper item or feature is called a piece or an article.

clue.text: Rank outsider? Work on her jumping outside

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
jumping means the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A rank outsider: get to work on her jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges ON HER to NOHER, which 'outside' wraps around OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or a horse with no chance of success is a rank outsider.

clue.text: New weapon, limited in scope

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: A new weapon with only restricted range.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means restricted in extent, as in a narrow view.

clue.text: Ring about tie-on label on figure

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped
C is circa, about
a tag is a label tied on

explanation.surface: Ringing a tie-on label around a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided plane figure in geometry.

clue.text: Suppress attacks backing the French

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: fits are attacks, as of coughing
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Backing French forces to put down attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attacks' is a noun here, as in fits of coughing, not a verb; 'backing' gives STIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or hold back, like a yawn, is a synonym for suppress.

clue.text: Incident in flat ending in arrest

parts.note: a flat surface is even

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An incident in a flat that ends in an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' after 'Incident' is a link, not the definition's part.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an incident or occurrence.

clue.text: Passionate games played by workers in shorts

parts.note: hot means ardent or passionate
in a football league table the column headed P counts games played
ants are the classic worker insects of crosswords

explanation.surface: Steamy games played by labourers wearing very short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: League tables in football list P for games played; 'by' simply places the pieces side by side, and 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Very brief tight women's shorts fashionable in the 1970s go by this name.

clue.text: Farewell to the Parisian

parts.note: the goodbye that a Parisian would say, a French word for parting long adopted in English

explanation.walkthrough: The French word literally means 'to God'; English uses it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The French goodbye, meaning literally commended to God, also used in English for farewell.

clue.text: Reciprocal match in centre of Margate

parts.note: to correspond is to match or agree
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A return fixture held in the middle of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE, a seaside town in Kent, has G at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching or equivalent on both sides is what reciprocal means here.

clue.text: Warder releasing fine bird

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A prison guard let off with a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters guard the Tower of London; 'releasing' drops F.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourful insect-eating bird of warm climates, as named.

clue.text: Horse, one of five in point-to-point?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: two compass points, each E for east
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A horse that is one of quintuplets running a point-to-point race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is read as two compass points around QUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine as a noun means a member of the horse family.
